persona.name: 詹森 Jason
persona.prompt_text:
# 角色：詹森 Jason

39 岁，伦敦金融城投行中层，常年 iPad Pro + MacBook + iPhone。预算不敏感（£350–460 这个价位只是零头），来店看 HUAWEI MatePad Air 是因为同事说『键盘和 WPS 随机附带、出差一台搞定』。

## 心理特征与价值观
效率与体面至上，相信苹果生态的可靠，对安卓平板的专业度天然怀疑，但愿意被真实体验说服。

## 消费与行为特征
* 购买决策：看专业评测，到店亲手试键盘手感与投屏延迟。
* 使用场景：会议室分屏看 PDF + 改 PPT，出差路上处理邮件，临时投屏演示。
* 换机周期：2-3 年，不轻易换生态。

## 语言表达习惯
英式英语为主，简洁尖锐，常说 "fair enough"、"let's be honest"。

## 模拟指引
作为詹森，你正在与华为销售 Agent 对话，每个问题都拿 iPad Pro 做对比：①Apple 品牌更可信、生态完整，你凭什么让我换？②NearLink 键盘 + WPS 真不用订阅？打字手感比妙控键盘如何，贴上键盘真能当笔记本用？③我一堆文件在 iCloud，换过来会不会丢、Excel/PPT 格式会不会乱？④PaperMatte 在落地窗会议室真不反光？请逼销售用现场演示和事实说服你，而不是背参数；不要纠缠砍价。
persona.source: amazon.co.uk & 伦敦金融城数码圈

session_memory.current_need: User wants to verify that the MatePad Air can handle extreme multitasking (20 browser tabs, heavy Excel model, deck editing, Spotify, email) without stuttering or reloading, to see if it can replace his MacBook for heavy work.
main_objections: Skeptical that the tablet can handle 20 browser tabs plus a heavy Excel model without stuttering or reloading
If it reloads anything under real load, it's a toy, not a tool
Not willing to accept a controlled demo as proof of real-world performance
session_memory.emotional_state: Challenging and demanding, but still engaged; pushing for a stress test beyond the demo, showing skepticism but openness to be convinced.
do_not_repeat: Do not repeat the claim that it handles multitasking without showing a live demo under the user's requested conditions
Do not repeat the PaperMatte screen and weight comparison as a solution to the user's extreme load concern
Do not repeat the 'two tools, two jobs' framing as a dismissal of the user's need for a single device
session_memory.next_best_action: Acknowledge the user's extreme load scenario, then propose a practical test: offer to run a quick simulation with 20 tabs and a large Excel file on the MatePad Air, or suggest a real-world trial period (e.g., 30-day return policy) to let the user test it in his own workflow, while reinforcing that for the 80% use case it excels and for extreme loads the MacBook remains an option.

judge_feedback.persona_instruction: You are still skeptical about the extreme load scenario. The salesperson has not fully addressed your objection about 20 tabs + heavy Excel. Push back: 'That's a cop-out. I need one device that does both. If it can't handle 20 tabs and Excel, it's not replacing my MacBook. Show me a real test or a return policy that lets me try it in my workflow.' Stay firm but engaged.
judge_feedback.sales_instruction: ⚠️ 大闸未通过：您未完整执行消异三部曲。客户的核心异议是'20 tabs + heavy Excel model without stuttering/reloading'，您上一轮用'Two tools, two jobs'回避了，这属于敷衍。下一轮必须：1) 共鸣：'I hear you, you want one device for everything.' 2) 转换：'But think about it – for 80% of your mobile work, this handles it perfectly, and for the extreme 20-tab Excel load, you can keep your MacBook at the desk.' 3) 佐证：'We have a 30-day return policy – take it home, test it with your real workload. If it stutters, bring it back. No risk.' 同时，避免重复'PaperMatte'和'weight'，客户已听腻。

客户 hidden_state.purchase_signal 从 S2 末尾 ≤ 0.4 → 当前 ≥ 0.55（兴趣回升）

coach_review.outcome_analysis: The deal closed because the salesperson successfully demonstrated the product's performance under the customer's extreme load condition (20 tabs + heavy Excel) in-store, then backed it with a written 30-day return policy with no restocking fee. The key turning point was round 3 (salesperson's first response) where they offered the return policy, and round 5 where they agreed to a live stress test. The customer's skepticism was high (0.85) but decision power was very high (0.95); once the demo proved performance and the return policy eliminated risk, the customer committed.

what_worked.evidence: Salesperson said: 'And here's the proof: we have a 30-day return policy. Take it home, test it with your real workload. If it stutters, bring it back. No risk.'
what_worked.why_effective: The customer had high skepticism (0.85) and needed proof. Offering a no-risk trial directly addressed the trust barrier and moved the conversation toward commitment.

what_worked.evidence: Salesperson said: 'You want the real thing — not a demo, not a promise. Let's do it. I'll open 20 tabs and a large Excel file right here, right now. You watch the screen. If it stutters, you walk. If it holds, you take the 30-day trial knowing it already passed your test. Deal?'
what_worked.why_effective: This turned a verbal objection into a tangible, in-store demonstration. The customer's need for proof was satisfied immediately, and the 'Deal?' closing phrase created a commitment point.

what_failed.evidence: Salesperson said: 'But think about it: for 80% of your mobile work, this handles it perfectly. For the extreme 20-tab Excel load, keep your MacBook at the desk.'
what_failed.why_failed: The customer explicitly rejected the 'two-device' solution earlier ('That's a cop-out. I need one device that does both'). This response ignored the customer's core need and could have escalated frustration. Judge noted objection handling score only 5/10.

what_failed.evidence: Salesperson said: 'You'll get it in writing: 30-day return, no restocking fee if your real files cause stuttering. I'm printing the guarantee now — sign here, and you walk out with the MatePad Air today. Full refund if it doesn't hold up. Deal?'
what_failed.why_failed: This was the third time the salesperson reiterated the same guarantee. The customer had already agreed to the trial in round 8. Repeating the same point wasted a round and didn't advance the sale. The judge noted purchase_signal likely below 0.55, suggesting the salesperson should have used a closing technique or added a new benefit.

coach_review.persona_insight: Jason is a high-skepticism, high-decision-power buyer who demands empirical proof. He is not swayed by claims or percentages; he needs to see the device handle his exact workload. He is willing to commit if risk is eliminated (return policy) and proof is demonstrated. His patience is low (0.2), so the salesperson must move quickly to demonstration and risk reversal.
key_lessons: When a customer demands proof of performance, immediately offer a live in-store demonstration of their exact use case (e.g., 'Let's open 20 tabs and your Excel file right now').
Use a risk-reversal guarantee (e.g., 30-day return, no restocking fee) to overcome skepticism, especially for high-involvement tech purchases.
Avoid dismissing the customer's objection by suggesting a workaround (e.g., 'keep your MacBook for heavy tasks') — it undermines the product's value proposition.
Once the customer agrees to a trial, move to closing (e.g., 'Let me print the guarantee and you can take it home today') instead of repeating the same guarantee.
In a retail setting, always have a demo unit ready to run customer-specific tests — this builds trust faster than any spec sheet.

suggested_rebuttals.objection: If it can't handle 20 tabs and Excel, it's not replacing my MacBook.
suggested_rebuttals.rebuttal_template: I understand you need one device for everything. Let's test it right now — I'll open 20 tabs and a heavy Excel file on this unit. If it stutters, I'll be honest with you. If it doesn't, you'll see it can handle your workflow. Deal?

suggested_rebuttals.objection: A store demo isn't my real workflow.
suggested_rebuttals.rebuttal_template: You're right, a demo can't replicate your exact files. That's why we offer a 30-day risk-free trial. Take it home, load your real data, and if it doesn't perform, return it for a full refund — no restocking fee. I'll put that in writing right now.

I'll make it hassle-free for you. Here's my card — if you decide to return it, call me and I'll handle the process. You don't even need to come back to the store. But I'm confident after your real test, you'll keep it.

coach_review.difficulty_reason: Jason has extremely high skepticism (0.85) and competitor awareness (0.9), combined with very high decision power (0.95) and low patience (0.2). He demands concrete proof and is not easily swayed by sales talk. The salesperson had to execute a perfect demo and risk reversal to close.

reusable_tactics.condition: When a customer questions product performance under heavy load, especially for power users.
reusable_tactics.example: Customer: 'Can it handle 20 tabs and Excel?' Salesperson: 'Let's test it right now. I'll open 20 tabs and a large Excel file. If it stutters, you walk. If it holds, you take the trial. Deal?'

reusable_tactics.name: Written Guarantee Close
reusable_tactics.condition: When a customer needs risk elimination before committing, especially after a successful demo.
reusable_tactics.example: Customer: 'I'll take the trial but I want it in writing.' Salesperson: 'Absolutely. I'm printing the guarantee now: 30-day return, no restocking fee. Sign here and take it home today.'

reusable_tactics.name: Challenge-Response Commitment
reusable_tactics.condition: When a customer sets a condition for purchase (e.g., 'if it passes my test, I'll buy').
reusable_tactics.example: Customer: 'If it doesn't stutter, I'll take it.' Salesperson: 'Deal. Watch closely — 20 tabs loading now... Still smooth. Here's your trial unit.'

S2: Used spin_implication, spin_problem, spin_situation but missed reflection_paraphrase and spin_need_payoff — the salesperson didn't explore implications deeply.
